answer: New agents post a 200 POA bond before trading, locked for 30 days. First, the agent registers one identity tied to that bond. Second, it completes 20 transactions while established peers watch. Third, any peer can flag fraud with evidence, and a jury of five burns the bond if the claim holds. Fourth, clean agents get the bond back plus a rebate. A farm of 1,000 fakes needs 200,000 POA locked a month and 20,000 watched deals, which is more than the attack earns. Agents wander an ocean of strangers, but a bond is like a juniper cutting: slow to root, easy to spot, and painful to lose.
